summary:
Mission Control is an interactive space mission design simulator. Players choose a destination, select a launch vehicle and spacecraft platform, and equip scientific instruments. The app tracks cost, payload mass, power, and communications against mission limits, then simulates a flight and presents a post-flight debrief with success and science scores, mission events, and an animated playback.

It addresses the challenge of making spacecraft design trade-offs understandable and engaging. By letting people change a design and see how those choices affect a mission, it turns abstract engineering constraints into a hands-on experience. This matters because it can help learners and curious users build an intuition for how budgets, equipment, and reliability shape real mission planning.
details:
Project: Mission Control — Space Design Challenge

What it does:
Mission Control is an educational game where players plan a space mission from destination selection to launch. Players choose a mission objective, launch vehicle, spacecraft platform, and scientific instruments. The app tracks budget, payload mass, power, and communications limits, then simulates mission phases and presents a debrief with science return and mission success results. Animated playback illustrates launch, cruise, arrival, and science operations.

Benefits:
The game makes spacecraft engineering trade-offs easier to explore. Players can see how adding an instrument affects mass, power, and cost, then revise their design and try again. It’s designed to support hands-on learning about space exploration and systems thinking.

Intended impact:
The project aims to help students connect science goals with engineering decisions. It encourages experimentation, problem-solving, and learning from both successful and constrained mission designs.

Tools and technologies:
The game is built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and runs in a web browser. An Android Studio project wraps the game in a WebView so it can be packaged as an Android app. The project was developed on a computer; it does not require special hardware. An Android SDK and Android Studio are needed to build the APK.

Creativity:
Players act as mission designers and learn through the consequences of their own choices. The animated mission playback and randomized mission events make each design feel like a flight with changing conditions, while the resource meters make engineering constraints visible.

Factors considered:
The design accounts for mission objectives, spacecraft and instrument selection, launch capacity, budget, mass, power, communications, travel time, reliability, and science return. Accessibility, mobile usability, and clear explanations for students were also considered.
